fields.sections.0.ko: The author was diagnosed with oral squamous cell carcinoma in May 2026, and this article consolidates practical lessons learned from that experience. It focuses on how to effectively navigate the healthcare system following a cancer diagnosis.
fields.sections.1.ko: In healthcare facility appointment systems, one must not passively wait but should actively request faster scheduling through phone calls. The author initially received an ENT appointment four weeks later, but after his wife suggested checking for cancellations, he was able to be seen that same week. This demonstrates that when individuals take proactive steps rather than relying on the system, outcomes can differ.
fields.sections.2.ko: The author notes that in conversations with AI models, most were guided toward emphasizing the possibility that it was not cancer. This is a warning that when referencing AI technology in medical diagnosis processes, its responses may be overly optimistic.
fields.sections.3.ko: He explains experiencing cases where some physicians postponed or failed to follow through on genetic testing. His surgeon said he would perform the test but ultimately referred him to an oncologist, causing the results to be delayed by several months. The key point is that the patient himself is more invested in his care than anyone else, so patients must take the initiative and follow up multiple times on next steps.
fields.sections.4.ko: Standard treatment flowcharts (NCCN guidelines) are publicly available for all cancer types, and patients can create member accounts and access them as non-specialists. Through this, one can independently understand options based on one's disease progression, and it is recommended to use AI to review options applicable to one's specific situation.
fields.sections.5.ko: He emphasizes with regret how important it is to consult beforehand with someone who has undergone the same surgery. While the surgeon's explanation was sufficient, the actual physical burden was far greater than anticipated. He also advises asking the doctor how many of these surgeries they perform annually and what the complication rate is.
fields.sections.6.ko: Even if satisfied with the current treatment plan, he strongly recommends obtaining a second opinion as quickly as possible. For this, he suggests not hesitating to book flights and hotel reservations, and seeking out major cancer treatment centers after the diagnosis is sufficiently confirmed. He proposes requesting a re-review of the biopsy results at such centers.
fields.sections.7.ko: After receiving treatment, he shares his experience of creating a folder on his Mac computer, recording clinical consultations and physician statements by voice, and then having AI write summaries and follow-up questions for the next appointment. He evaluates it as useful that over time, he could manage the treatment process by referring to these records.
fields.sections.8.ko: He introduces the usefulness of resources from the Sijbrandij Foundation, which GitLab co-founder Sid built directly when facing situations outside standard treatment scope, and a question list directed at medical professionals. He recommends scheduling a consultation with this institution.
fields.sections.9.ko: From Hacker News comments, advice raised that if one is within 2–3 hours of a major cancer center, one should go there rather than a local hospital. One can refer to U.S. News cancer hospital rankings to select, and top centers typically accept insurance, so if vacation and hotel reservations are necessary, one should do so. According to the author's experience, at MD Anderson, the physician could directly consult with a pathologist by phone within 20 minutes after the visit to answer questions, whereas at a local hospital it would have taken several days or no answer would have been obtained.
fields.caveat: This article is based on the author's personal experience and may not apply equally to all cancer types and healthcare systems, so advice from local medical professionals and specialized institutions should always take priority.
